title: How a Spark Plug Works in 60 Seconds ⚡🔥 #shorts
description:
A spark plug fires with thousands of volts, jumping a tiny gap to light the fuel inside a gasoline engine. An ignition coil boosts the car's 12 volt battery, the spark ignites the air and fuel, and the blast pushes the piston down. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#sparkplug #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: At 3,000 rpm, each spark plug in a four-stroke engine fires about *1,500 times* a minute.

steps.label: Battery
steps.text: It all starts with the car's *12 volt* battery. That's far too weak to make a spark.

steps.label: Coil
steps.text: An *ignition coil* boosts it to tens of thousands of volts.

steps.label: Gap
steps.text: The voltage races down the center electrode and jumps a *tiny gap*, about one millimeter wide.

steps.label: Ignition
steps.text: That spark lights the *air and fuel* squeezed into the cylinder.

steps.label: Power
steps.text: The burning gas expands and *pushes the piston* down, turning the engine.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Boost, *spark*, bang. Follow Inside 60 for more.
